org: PROMYS (Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists), Boston University

name.ar: برنامج PROMYS 2027 (جامعة بوسطن)

deadline_note: PROMYS says the 2027 application launches in January; 2026 deadline was 27 Feb (11:59 pm EST). Exact 2027 dates not yet posted; deadline estimated from the 2026 pattern.

summary.en: A six-week summer programme at Boston University where about 80 mathematically gifted teenagers explore number theory through hard problem sets. Students from anywhere can apply; need-based aid is available.
summary.ka: ექვსკვირიანი საზაფხულო პროგრამა ბოსტონის უნივერსიტეტში, სადაც დაახლოებით 80 მათემატიკურად ნიჭიერი მოზარდი რთული ამოცანების მეშვეობით რიცხვთა თეორიას სწავლობს. განაცხადის შეტანა ნებისმიერი ქვეყნიდან შეიძლება; ხელმისაწვდომია საჭიროებაზე დაფუძნებული დახმარება.
summary.ar: برنامج صيفي لستة أسابيع في جامعة بوسطن يستكشف فيه نحو 80 مراهقاً موهوباً في الرياضيات نظرية الأعداد عبر مسائل صعبة. يمكن التقديم من أي بلد مع توفر منح حسب الحاجة المالية.

about.en:
PROMYS is one of the oldest and most respected summer mathematics programmes in the world. Held at Boston University's Department of Mathematics, it gives about 60 first-year students (plus returning students) six weeks of intensive work on number theory: daily problem sets, lectures, advanced seminars and mentoring from undergraduate counsellors and research mathematicians. The aim is to learn to think like a mathematician, not to race through a syllabus.

Applicants must solve a set of challenging problems as the core of the application, submitted together with a transcript, short answers and a recommendation from a maths teacher or mentor. Admission is selective but open to students worldwide aged 14–18 who have completed at least 9th grade. Students in China can apply for full Yongren Fellowships; European residents aged 16+ may choose PROMYS Europe in Oxford instead (not both in the same year).

en: Classic number-theory immersion with research mathematicians and counsellors
Admission is based mainly on solving a challenging problem set
Need-based financial aid; full Yongren Fellowships for students in China

eligibility.en: Students aged 14–18 by the start of the programme who have completed at least 9th grade (or equivalent) and are not yet enrolled at university. International students are welcome; good English is needed. Applicants may apply to PROMYS or PROMYS Europe, not both, in the same summer.

en: Watch the PROMYS application page from January 2027, when the 2027 problem set is published
Work on the problem set and write up your solutions as one PDF
Complete the online form with short answers and upload your school transcript
Ask a maths teacher or mentor to submit the recommendation form (due a few days after the deadline)
If you need aid, have a parent complete the financial aid form by mid-March
Decisions are emailed by the end of April

costs.en: Programme fee covers tuition, room and board in Boston (amount published with the application; check the site). Need-based financial aid is available, and some fellowships cover all costs including travel.

score_reason: Elite maths programme open to international students with need-based aid; application opens January.

name.ar: برنامج Ross للرياضيات 2027

duration.ar: 6 أسابيع (من منتصف يونيو إلى أواخر يوليو)

deadline_note: 2026 deadline was 8 March; the 2027 application has not been posted yet. Date estimated from the 2026 pattern; 2026 sites were Otterbein University (Ohio) and Rose-Hulman (Indiana).

summary.en: A six-week summer immersion in number theory for motivated pre-college students, run at two US campuses. International students are accepted every year.
summary.ka: ექვსკვირიანი საზაფხულო პროგრამა რიცხვთა თეორიაში მოტივირებული სკოლის მოსწავლეებისთვის აშშ-ის ორ კამპუსზე. ყოველწლიურად იღებენ საერთაშორისო სტუდენტებსაც.
summary.ar: برنامج صيفي مكثف لستة أسابيع في نظرية الأعداد لطلاب ما قبل الجامعة المتحمسين في حرمين جامعيين أمريكيين، ويُقبل فيه طلاب دوليون كل عام.

about.en:
The Ross Program, founded by Arnold Ross in 1957, is a six-week residential summer course in which students discover number theory for themselves through daily problem sets, lectures and discussion with counsellors. The motto is 'Think deeply of simple things'. In 2026 it ran from 14 June to 24 July at Otterbein University in Columbus, Ohio and at Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology in Indiana.

Most first-year students are 15–18. International students are admitted every year (several per year) and need reasonable English fluency; the programme is treated as a 'mathematical vacation' so a visitor visa usually suffices. The application includes short essays, a video, a teacher recommendation, a transcript and solutions to challenging maths problems.

en: Legendary programme in number theory with a 'learn by discovering' approach
Two campuses in the US Midwest
Need-based scholarships available

eligibility.en: Motivated pre-college students, typically aged 15–18 (occasionally 14 or recent graduates). International applicants are welcome and need good English.

en: Check rossprogram.org from winter 2026/27 for the 2027 application and problem set
Solve the admission problems and write up your solutions
Prepare short essays, a short video, your transcript and a teacher recommendation
Submit before the deadline (8 March in 2026)
If admitted, ask about need-based scholarships

costs.en: Programme fee USD 7,500 (2026) covering six weeks of room, board, instruction and course costs. Need-based scholarships available; travel is rarely covered for international students.

score_reason: Top maths summer programme that admits internationals; 2027 dates not yet published.

name.ar: مخيم Canada/USA Mathcamp للرياضيات 2027

deadline_note: Mathcamp announces 2027 dates and campus in December 2026. In 2026 the application opened 12 Jan and closed 23 Feb with the Qualifying Quiz; 2027 dates estimated from that pattern.

summary.en: A five-week summer camp for mathematically talented 13–18-year-olds from around the world, with university-level classes chosen by students. There is no application fee and generous need-based aid, including for international students.
summary.ka: ხუთკვირიანი საზაფხულო ბანაკი მთელი მსოფლიოდან მათემატიკურად ნიჭიერი 13–18 წლის მოზარდებისთვის, უნივერსიტეტის დონის კურსებით, რომლებსაც მონაწილეები თავად ირჩევენ. განაცხადი უფასოა და საერთაშორისო სტუდენტებისთვისაც არის დიდი ფინანსური დახმარება.
summary.ar: مخيم صيفي لخمسة أسابيع للموهوبين في الرياضيات بعمر 13–18 عاماً من جميع أنحاء العالم، مع مواد بمستوى جامعي يختارها الطلاب. لا توجد رسوم تقديم وتتوفر منح سخية حسب الحاجة حتى للطلاب الدوليين.

about.en:
Mathcamp is a five-week residential summer programme where about 120 students choose from dozens of university-level classes (combinatorics, topology, cryptography, analysis and more), work on projects, and live in a campus community with mathematicians. In 2026 it ran 28 June – 2 August at Champlain College, Burlington, Vermont; the 2027 location and dates are announced in December.

Admission is based mainly on the Qualifying Quiz, a set of challenging problems that you solve at home and submit with your application. There is no application fee. The base fee was USD 7,500 in 2026, but over USD 100,000 a year goes to need-based scholarships: international students can receive full scholarships and travel grants.

en: Students design their own timetable from dozens of advanced maths classes
Admission through a take-home Qualifying Quiz; no application fee
Full scholarships and travel grants available to international students

eligibility.en: Mathematically talented students aged 13–18 from any country. Good English required. Admission is by application and the Qualifying Quiz.

en: Sign up for the Mathcamp mailing list and check the site in December 2026 for 2027 dates
When the 2027 Qualifying Quiz is published, solve as many problems as you can and write full solutions
Fill in the online application (essay, recommendation) by the deadline (late February in 2026)
Apply for financial aid at the same time if needed
Decisions are announced in mid-April

costs.en: 2026 base fee USD 7,500 covering tuition, room, board, activities and airport transfers; final fee after aid ranges from 0 to 7,500. No application fee. Need-based aid, full scholarships and travel grants available to international students.

score_reason: Top maths camp, worldwide eligibility, no application fee and aid for internationals.

org: Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics (HCSSiM)

name.ar: برنامج HCSSiM 2027 للدراسات الصيفية في الرياضيات

duration.ar: 6 أسابيع (من أواخر يونيو إلى أوائل أغسطس)

deadline_note: 2026 new-application deadline was 17 April with the 'Interesting Test' due 25 April. HCSSiM is continuing as an independent programme and will announce its new 2027 campus in late 2026; dates estimated from 2026.

summary.en: A six-week intensive summer maths programme for talented high-school students, known for proof-based workshops and its 'Interesting Test' admission puzzle. Ample financial aid is available.
summary.ka: ექვსკვირიანი ინტენსიური საზაფხულო მათემატიკური პროგრამა ნიჭიერი მოსწავლეებისთვის, ცნობილი დამტკიცებებზე დაფუძნებული სემინარებით და მისაღები „საინტერესო ტესტით“. ხელმისაწვდომია ფინანსური დახმარება.
summary.ar: برنامج صيفي مكثف لستة أسابيع في الرياضيات لطلاب الثانوية الموهوبين، يشتهر بورش العمل القائمة على البراهين واختبار القبول المسمى «الاختبار الممتع». تتوفر مساعدات مالية واسعة.

about.en:
HCSSiM has run since 1971 and immerses talented and highly motivated high-school students in university-level mathematics for six weeks: morning workshops on proofs and problem solving, afternoon problem sessions, evening maxi- and mini-courses and a close-knit residential community. Many alumni became research mathematicians.

In 2026 it ran 28 June – 8 August on the Hampshire College campus. Hampshire College is closing, but HCSSiM continues as an independent organisation and will announce its 2027 campus in late 2026. Applicants submit an application and the 'Interesting Test', a set of puzzles that shows how you think.

en: Proof-based workshops that teach how mathematicians actually work
Admission puzzle ('Interesting Test') rather than grades
Ample need-based financial aid

eligibility.en: Talented, highly motivated high-school students. The page does not restrict nationality; international applicants should check visa and travel logistics.

en: Check hcssim.org in late 2026 for the 2027 campus and dates
Download and work on the Interesting Test
Submit the online application (deadline mid-April in 2026)
Submit the Interesting Test about a week later
Apply for financial aid via hcssim.org/money if needed

costs.en: 2026 fee USD 7,208 (tuition, room and board). Ample need-based aid available.

score_reason: Respected maths programme with aid; 2027 campus to be confirmed.

name.ar: مخيم الرياضيات في جامعة ستانفورد (SUMaC) 2027

deadline_note: 2026 aid deadline was 9 Feb with the admission deadline in the same period; 2027 application not yet open. Dates estimated from the 2026 pattern; join the mailing list for exact dates.

summary.en: Stanford's advanced summer maths programme for rising juniors and seniors worldwide: abstract algebra, number theory or algebraic topology, residential on campus or live online. Need-based aid is open to international students.
summary.ka: Stanford-ის მოწინავე საზაფხულო მათემატიკური პროგრამა მთელი მსოფლიოს მე-10 და მე-11 კლასელებისთვის: აბსტრაქტული ალგებრა, რიცხვთა თეორია ან ალგებრული ტოპოლოგია, კამპუსზე ან ონლაინ. საჭიროებაზე დაფუძნებული დახმარება საერთაშორისო სტუდენტებისთვისაც ხელმისაწვდომია.
summary.ar: برنامج ستانفورد الصيفي المتقدم في الرياضيات لطلاب الصفين العاشر والحادي عشر من كل العالم: الجبر المجرد أو نظرية الأعداد أو الطوبولوجيا الجبرية، حضورياً أو مباشرة عبر الإنترنت. المساعدات حسب الحاجة متاحة للطلاب الدوليين.

about.en:
SUMaC introduces strong high-school students to university-level abstract mathematics through lectures, problem sessions and a research-style group project, taught by Stanford-affiliated instructors. In 2026 it offered a 4-week residential session on the Stanford campus (21 June – 17 July, 40 places) and two 3-week online sessions (64 places each) with live classes.

It is open to students from around the world currently in grades 10–11. Fees are high (2026: USD 8,950 residential, USD 3,750 online), but Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies offers need-based financial aid to domestic and international applicants, and applying for aid does not affect admission.

en: University-level abstract algebra, number theory or topology with group research projects
Residential on Stanford campus or live online
Need-based aid available to international students

eligibility.en: Students in grades 10–11 (rising juniors and seniors) from any country with strong maths preparation and good English.

en: Join the SUMaC mailing list for 2027 dates
Submit the online application with transcripts, recommendation and admission problems
Request financial aid in the application if needed and submit documents via SSS by the aid deadline (early February in 2026)
Decisions follow in spring

costs.en: 2026: USD 8,950 residential (housing, meals, supplies, trips) or USD 3,750 online. Financial aid application fee USD 60 (waivers available). Need-based aid for domestic and international students.

score_reason: Prestigious and international-friendly but expensive without aid.

name.ar: برنامج AwesomeMath الصيفي 2027 (عبر الإنترنت)

deadline_note: 2026 cycle opened 15 Dec 2025 with an early deadline 14 Jan, regular rounds Feb–Mar and a final deadline 26 May. 2027 dates estimated from that pattern; later rounds cost more.

summary.en: A three-week online olympiad-style maths programme for students aged about 12–18 from around the world, with live daily classes. Admission is by an entrance test; earlier applications get lower tuition.
summary.ka: სამკვირიანი ონლაინ ოლიმპიადური მათემატიკის პროგრამა მთელი მსოფლიოს დაახლოებით 12–18 წლის მოსწავლეებისთვის, ყოველდღიური პირდაპირი გაკვეთილებით. მიღება ხდება მისაღები ტესტით; ადრე შეტანილ განაცხადზე სწავლის საფასური ნაკლებია.
summary.ar: برنامج رياضيات أولمبيادي عبر الإنترنت لمدة ثلاثة أسابيع لطلاب بعمر 12–18 تقريباً من جميع أنحاء العالم، مع دروس مباشرة يومية. القبول عبر اختبار دخول، والرسوم أقل للمتقدمين مبكراً.

about.en:
AwesomeMath, founded by olympiad coach Titu Andreescu, runs an intensive online summer programme in problem solving: number theory, algebra, combinatorics and geometry courses at four levels, taught live Monday to Friday by an international faculty. In 2026 there were three sessions (8–26 June, 29 June – 17 July, 20 July – 7 August).

Admission is by an entrance test (Part I for levels 1–2, Part II for levels 3–4). It is a good preparation path for national olympiads and AMC/AIME-style competitions and is open to students worldwide.

en: Olympiad-style courses at four levels taught by experienced coaches
Three online sessions to choose from
Early-application discount

eligibility.en: Middle- and high-school students roughly 12–18 years old, from any country, who pass the admission test.

en: Check the AwesomeMath site in mid-December 2026 for 2027 enrolment
Take the admission test (choose Part I or II according to your level)
Submit the application by the early deadline (mid-January) for the best price, or by later rounds
Choose your session and courses after admission

costs.en: Tuition varies by session and application round (see the site); each course includes a free book. Online, so no travel or housing costs.

score_reason: Accessible online olympiad training worldwide, but paid.

name.ar: برنامج الطلاب الصيفي في CERN لعام 2027

deadline_note: CERN states applications must arrive no later than the end of January; the 2027 vacancy is not yet posted on careers.cern (check from November/December). Date is the usual end-of-January pattern.

summary.en: Undergraduate and master's students in physics, engineering, computer science or maths spend a summer working in a CERN team, with a lecture programme on particle physics. CERN pays a daily allowance and may cover travel; all nationalities can apply.
summary.ka: ფიზიკის, ინჟინერიის, კომპიუტერული მეცნიერების ან მათემატიკის ბაკალავრიატისა და მაგისტრატურის სტუდენტები ზაფხულს CERN-ის გუნდში მუშაობენ და ნაწილაკთა ფიზიკის ლექციებს ესწრებიან. CERN იხდის დღიურ ანაზღაურებას და შესაძლოა მგზავრობაც დაფაროს; განაცხადის შეტანა ყველა ქვეყნის მოქალაქეს შეუძლია.
summary.ar: يقضي طلاب البكالوريوس والماجستير في الفيزياء والهندسة وعلوم الحاسوب والرياضيات الصيف في العمل ضمن فريق في CERN مع برنامج محاضرات في فيزياء الجسيمات. يدفع CERN بدلاً يومياً وقد يغطي السفر، والتقديم مفتوح لجميع الجنسيات.

about.en:
The CERN Summer Student Programme brings several hundred students to the world's largest particle physics laboratory near Geneva each summer. Each student joins an experimental, theoretical, computing or engineering team for 8–13 weeks, works on a real project, and follows a dedicated lecture series given by CERN scientists, plus visits to experiments and a student poster session.

CERN says all nationalities are welcome to apply (students from Canada, Japan and the US apply through their national schemes). Successful candidates receive a net subsistence allowance of CHF 94 per calendar day, and travel to and from Geneva may be covered. It is one of the most prestigious summer experiences for anyone considering a career in physics or scientific computing.

en: Work on a real project in a CERN team for 2–3 months
Dedicated summer lecture programme on particle physics and computing
Daily allowance of CHF 94 (net); travel may be covered

eligibility.en: Bachelor's or master's students (not PhD) in physics, engineering, computer science or mathematics with at least 6 semesters of full-time study completed by the start, still enrolled full-time, with good English. Must not have attended before or worked at CERN for more than 3 months. All nationalities welcome; Canadian, Japanese and US students use their national schemes.

en: Check careers.cern/summer from late 2026 for the 2027 Summer Student vacancy
Prepare a CV, motivation letter and transcripts
Arrange two reference letters (referees submit online)
Submit before the end of January 2027
Selection results are usually communicated in spring

costs.en: Net subsistence allowance of CHF 94 per calendar day (health insurance deducted). Travel to/from Geneva may be covered depending on circumstances. No fee to apply.

score_reason: World-famous funded summer research programme open to all nationalities.

name.ar: برنامج الطلاب الصيفي في DESY لعام 2027

deadline_note: DESY says the 2027 programme is 'currently in preparation'; deadline and application link not yet published. Previous cycles closed around the end of January; treat the date as an estimate and check the site.

summary.en: A paid 7.5-week summer research programme at one of Europe's leading accelerator and photon-science labs, in Hamburg or Zeuthen near Berlin. Free hostel accommodation, a daily salary and travel support are provided.
summary.ka: ანაზღაურებადი 7,5-კვირიანი საზაფხულო კვლევითი პროგრამა ევროპის ერთ-ერთ წამყვან ამაჩქარებლისა და ფოტონური მეცნიერების ლაბორატორიაში, ჰამბურგში ან ბერლინთან ახლოს მდებარე ცოიტენში. უზრუნველყოფილია უფასო საცხოვრებელი, დღიური ანაზღაურება და მგზავრობის დაფარვა.
summary.ar: برنامج بحثي صيفي مدفوع لمدة 7.5 أسابيع في أحد أبرز مختبرات المسرعات وعلوم الفوتونات في أوروبا، في هامبورغ أو زويتن قرب برلين. يتم توفير سكن مجاني وراتب يومي ودعم للسفر.

about.en:
DESY's Summer Student Programme lets undergraduates in physics and related fields (scientific computing, engineering) join a research group at DESY in Hamburg or Zeuthen for 7.5 weeks. Students work 39 hours a week, combining a research project with a lecture series on particle physics, accelerator physics, photon science and astroparticle physics, and present their results at the end.

The programme is international and fully supported: free accommodation in the DESY hostel for the whole stay, a salary of EUR 28.50 per day and at least partial reimbursement of travel costs. The 2027 call is being prepared; watch the website for the opening.

en: Research project at a world-class accelerator and photon-science centre
Lecture programme across particle, accelerator and photon science
Free accommodation, EUR 28.50/day salary and travel reimbursement

eligibility.en: Undergraduate students of physics or related fields (scientific computing, engineering) from any country, typically before their master's thesis. Good English required.

en: Check summerstudents.desy.de for the 2027 call
Prepare CV, transcript, motivation statement and recommendation letter(s)
Choose your preferred research areas
Submit the online application before the deadline (usually end of January)

costs.en: Free DESY hostel accommodation, salary of EUR 28.50 per day, and at least partial reimbursement of travel costs.

score_reason: Funded, international research summer at a top lab; 2027 call pending.

name.en: EPFL Life Sciences Summer Research Program 2027
name.ka: EPFL-ის სიცოცხლის მეცნიერებების საზაფხულო კვლევითი პროგრამა 2027
name.ar: برنامج EPFL الصيفي للبحث في علوم الحياة 2027

deadline_note: Official page: deadline 15 November 2026, 23:59 CET; applications open now. Programme dates 5 July – 27 August 2027.

summary.en: Eight weeks of full-time lab research at EPFL for 20–25 international undergraduates in life sciences. A CHF 3,600 stipend covers housing and living costs, and most travel is reimbursed.
summary.ka: რვაკვირიანი სრული განაკვეთის ლაბორატორიული კვლევა EPFL-ში 20–25 საერთაშორისო სტუდენტისთვის სიცოცხლის მეცნიერებებში. 3 600 შვეიცარიული ფრანკის სტიპენდია ფარავს საცხოვრებელსა და ხარჯებს, მგზავრობის უმეტესი ნაწილიც ანაზღაურდება.

about.en:
The Summer Research Program of EPFL's School of Life Sciences places international bachelor's and first-year master's students in an EPFL research group in Lausanne (or Geneva) for eight weeks of hands-on lab work, from 5 July to 27 August 2027. Fields include biology, biophysics, chemistry, bioengineering, bioinformatics and quantitative biology.

Each student receives CHF 3,600 for the two months (housing in shared student accommodation near campus is deducted in advance, leaving about CHF 1,700 to live on), and travel to Switzerland is reimbursed up to CHF 1,000 for overseas flights or CHF 500 for shorter trips. Only 20–25 students are selected, so a clear research motivation and a strong referee letter matter.

CHF 3,600 stipend plus travel reimbursement
Only 20–25 places: small, well-supported cohort

Prepare your transcript and short-answer essays
Ask a referee to write a letter
Apply on the EPFL recruiting portal by 15 November 2026, 23:59 CET

about.en:
Summer@EPFL invites strong bachelor's and master's students from around the world to spend two to three months (usually between May and September, dates agreed with the host lab) doing research in one of the labs of EPFL's School of Computer and Communication Sciences in Lausanne: machine learning, systems, security, theory, networking, signal processing and more.

Fellows receive CHF 1,800 per month (prorated) plus a refund of travel costs (economy flight or second-class train). Selection is highly competitive and based on academic results; many fellows go on to PhD programmes at EPFL and other top universities.

en: Research internship in a top-ranked computer science school
CHF 1,800/month stipend plus travel refund
Strong pathway to EPFL master's and PhD programmes

eligibility.en: Bachelor's (at least 2nd year) or master's students, or equivalent, in computer science, computer engineering, telecommunications or electrical engineering. PhD students are not eligible. Open worldwide.

Prepare CV, transcripts and a statement of interest; identify labs you would like to join
Arrange recommendation letters
Submit the online application by 29 November 2026 (AoE)
Decisions are emailed before 25 January 2027

costs.en: CHF 1,800 per month, prorated to the actual duration, plus refund of travel costs (2nd-class train or economy flight). No application fee mentioned.

about.en:
The VBC Summer School places students in labs at the Vienna BioCenter institutes (IMP, IMBA, GMI, Max Perutz Labs) for nine weeks of full-time research in molecular biology, neuroscience, structural biology, plant biology, computational biology and related fields. Alongside the lab project there are lectures, soft-skills sessions and a final symposium where students present their work.

It is open worldwide to students with at least two years of life-science university study and at least three months of research experience. There is no application fee. Participants get free student accommodation, a stipend of EUR 1,400 after tax and medical insurance.

en: Nine weeks in a leading Vienna life-science lab
Free housing, EUR 1,400 stipend and insurance
No application fee; open to students worldwide

Rank three lab heads you would like to work with
Upload official proof of enrolment and transcripts
Start your application by 8 January and submit by 11 January 2027, 23:59 CET

about.en:
UTRIP (UTokyo Research Internship Program) brings undergraduates from universities outside Japan to the Graduate School of Science for six consecutive weeks of full-time research in physics, chemistry, biology, earth and planetary science, astronomy, mathematics or information science, plus Japanese culture activities.

Participants receive the GSS-UTRIP Scholarship: a one-off allowance on arrival (JPY 140,000 for Asia/Oceania, 160,000 for Europe/North America, 170,000 for Latin America, Africa and the Middle East) meant to cover the round-trip flight and local costs, and free housing for the 43-night stay. Students at US universities can instead apply for the FUTI award (up to USD 2,000 plus housing).

en: Six weeks in a University of Tokyo science lab
Scholarship of JPY 140,000–170,000 plus free housing
Priority to 3rd-year students of 4-year programmes

eligibility.en: Undergraduates who have completed at least one year of a bachelor's degree at a university outside Japan, in a natural science or related field, with interest in a scientific career. English test (TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent) required unless English is your first language or you have 8 years of English-medium education. Health insurance required.

en: Check the UTRIP 'What's New' page in November 2026 for the 2027 call
Choose labs/research areas of interest
Prepare transcript, essays and English test score
Ask a recommender to submit the recommendation form (about a week after the deadline)
Submit online before the deadline (early January in 2026)

costs.en: GSS-UTRIP Scholarship: one-time JPY 140,000–170,000 depending on region, covering airfare and daily costs; free housing for 43 nights. Insurance is your responsibility.

summary.ar: تدريب بحثي لمدة 4–6 أشهر في أي مختبر في OIST في أوكيناوا، لطلاب السنوات الأخيرة من البكالوريوس وطلاب الماجستير والخريجين الجدد من كل العالم. يغطي OIST تذكرة الطيران والسكن ويدفع مكافأة يومية.

about.en:
OIST is an English-language graduate university in Okinawa with an interdisciplinary research culture across physics, chemistry, biology, neuroscience, marine science, mathematics and computing. Its Research Internship lets students join a research unit of their choice for 4 to 6 months; the Fall 2027 round covers placements between 1 October 2027 and 31 March 2028.

Support is generous: one round-trip air ticket, furnished housing on or off campus, a stipend of JPY 2,400 per working day, visa help and a shuttle-bus pass. The internship is also a common route into OIST's fully funded PhD programme.

en: Choose any OIST research unit across the sciences
Flight, housing and JPY 2,400/working-day stipend covered
Common pathway to OIST's funded PhD

eligibility.en: Students in the last two years of a bachelor's degree or any year of a master's degree (in Japan or abroad), and bachelor's/master's graduates. Current or former PhD students are not eligible. Home-institution approval needed if enrolled.

en: Browse OIST research units and pick the host you want
Prepare transcripts, a 250-word statement of purpose, CV, passport scan and ID photo
Ask 1–3 professors to submit recommendation letters (at least one must arrive before you submit)
Pay the JPY 5,000 application fee and submit by 15 April 2027 (23:59 JST)
Results are announced in mid-June 2027

costs.en: Free for interns: round-trip flight, furnished housing and a stipend of JPY 2,400 per working day. Application fee JPY 5,000 (non-refundable).

summary.ka: ჩრდილოეთ ამერიკის, ბრიტანეთისა და ირლანდიის უნივერსიტეტების ბაკალავრები ზაფხულს გერმანიის უნივერსიტეტებსა და ინსტიტუტებში დოქტორანტების კვლევით ასისტენტებად ატარებენ. DAAD იხდის ყოველთვიურ სტიპენდიას; გერმანული ენა საჭირო არ არის.
summary.ar: يقضي طلاب البكالوريوس في جامعات أمريكا الشمالية وبريطانيا وأيرلندا الصيف مساعدين بحثيين لطلاب الدكتوراه في جامعات ومعاهد ألمانية. تدفع DAAD منحة شهرية ولا تُشترط معرفة الألمانية.

about.en:
RISE Germany (Research Internships in Science and Engineering) matches undergraduates with research groups across Germany for a three-month summer internship. Students pick projects from an online database of offers in biology, chemistry, physics, earth sciences and engineering, and work alongside a doctoral student who acts as mentor. The working language is English.

DAAD pays a monthly stipend towards living costs, host institutions help with housing, and interns join a DAAD network meeting. Eligibility depends on where you study, not your passport: international students enrolled at universities in the US, Canada, the UK or Ireland can apply.

en: Hands-on research with a PhD mentor at a German university or institute
Monthly DAAD stipend; housing help from hosts
No German required

eligibility.en: Undergraduates enrolled at universities in the USA, Canada, the UK or Ireland studying biology, chemistry, physics, earth sciences, engineering or a closely related field. Nationality is not restricted; students elsewhere are not eligible.

en: Browse internship offers in the RISE database
Register on the application portal and choose up to three projects
Upload CV, transcript and motivation letters
Ask referees to submit letters by 15 December 2026
Submit by 30 November 2026; hosts rank applicants in January

costs.en: DAAD monthly stipend for three months (amount set by DAAD) towards living costs; hosts assist with housing. No fee.

about.en:
Amgen Scholars is a summer undergraduate research programme funded by the Amgen Foundation. In the Asia programme, each host university places scholars in a lab for about 8–10 weeks of full-time research, with seminars and networking, and all scholars meet at a symposium in Japan in August (travel, room and board for the symposium are covered).

You do not need to study at the host university or be a citizen of an Asian country: you must be enrolled as an undergraduate at a university anywhere in Asia as defined by the UN (Eastern, South-Eastern, Central, Southern and Western Asia, which includes countries such as Georgia, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE). Each host has its own application and its own package for housing, meals and travel, so read the host page carefully.

en: Full-time lab research at a leading Asian university
Open to undergraduates at any university in Asia, including Georgia and the Gulf
All-expenses-paid Amgen Scholars symposium in Japan

eligibility.en: Undergraduates enrolled at a degree-granting university in Asia (UN definition, including Western Asia), who have completed at least their first year, are not graduating before the programme and will return for at least one more term. Strong academic record, English proficiency (e.g. TOEFL iBT 72 / IELTS 5.5 if not a native speaker) and interest in a PhD. Citizenship of an Asian country is not required.

en: Check the host university's Amgen Scholars page for its application form (applications open from November)
Prepare your official transcript and personal statement
Ask a professor for a recommendation letter
Submit the separate application for each host you choose by 1 February 2027
Applicants are notified by early April 2027

costs.en: Housing, meals and travel support vary by host (check the host page); symposium travel, room and board are covered. No tuition.

score_reason: Funded research summer open to students at universities anywhere in Asia.

summary.en: Ten weeks of original research in biology, neuroscience, cancer, genomics or quantitative biology at the famous Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory. Students get a USD 7,000 stipend plus free room and board.
summary.ka: ათკვირიანი ორიგინალური კვლევა ბიოლოგიაში, ნეირომეცნიერებაში, ონკოლოგიაში, გენომიკაში ან რაოდენობრივ ბიოლოგიაში ცნობილ Cold Spring Harbor-ის ლაბორატორიაში. სტუდენტები იღებენ 7 000 დოლარის სტიპენდიას და უფასო საცხოვრებელსა და კვებას.
summary.ar: عشرة أسابيع من البحث الأصلي في علم الأحياء وعلوم الأعصاب والسرطان والجينوم والأحياء الكمية في مختبر Cold Spring Harbor الشهير. يحصل الطلاب على منحة 7,000 دولار مع سكن وطعام مجانيين.

about.en:
The URP brings about 25 undergraduates to Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory on Long Island, home of eight Nobel laureates, for a mentored original research project with a CSHL faculty member. Alongside lab work there are seminars, a journal club, career discussions and a final symposium. Students with engineering, chemistry, computer science, maths or physics backgrounds are welcome, not only biologists.

CSHL says students of any nationality are eligible and no TOEFL/IELTS is required, but foreign students normally must be enrolled full-time at a US college or (in limited cases) at a foreign university with a CSHL agreement. Participants receive a USD 7,000 stipend and free housing in campus cabins and meals.

en: Original research project with a CSHL faculty mentor
USD 7,000 stipend plus room and board
No English test required

eligibility.en: Current sophomores and juniors (or equivalent) planning to continue their degree after the summer, with a strong science background. Any nationality, but foreign students must normally be enrolled full-time at a US college, or in limited cases at a foreign university with a CSHL agreement.

en: Complete the online URP application with personal statement (you may name 2–3 desired mentors)
Ask two referees to upload letters before the deadline
Submit everything by 15 January 2027, 23:59 PST
Notifications are sent by the end of March

costs.en: Stipend USD 7,000; room and board covered. No tuition.

score_reason: Elite funded biology research summer; mostly for students at US universities.

about.en:
Founded in 1959, LIYSF is a 14-day residential STEM forum held each July in London. Participants attend principal lectures from leading scientists (past speakers include Nobel laureates), specialist lectures, visits to research labs, universities and companies, and present their own projects at the Science Bazaar, all while living on a university campus with students from around 70 countries.

The 2027 forum runs 18–31 July in a hybrid format (on campus in London or online). It is a paid programme; some national organisations and schools sponsor delegates, so ask your national science body or school about nominations.

en: Lectures from world-leading scientists and visits to top labs
Students from about 70 countries
Present your own research at the Science Bazaar

eligibility.en: Students aged 16–21 with a strong interest in science, from any country, with good English.

Click 'Apply now' and complete the online application
Ask your school or national science organisation whether they sponsor delegates
Pay the fee once accepted and arrange a UK visa if needed

about.en:
SSRP places high-school students in research labs at The Rockefeller University, a biomedical research institution with many Nobel laureates. Over seven weeks (9am–5pm, Monday to Friday) students carry out a mentored research project, take part in workshops on experimental design and science communication, and present their findings at the end.

Participation and application are free, and NYC transit is covered; need-based stipends may be awarded. Students outside the US are encouraged to apply, but RockEDU cannot help with travel, accommodation or visas, so it suits international students who have family or a safe place to stay in New York.

en: Real biomedical research in Rockefeller University labs
Free to apply and attend; NYC transit card provided
Need-based stipends possible

Ask recommenders to submit letters before the deadline
Submit by 4 January 2027, 5:00 pm ET

Residential, commuter or online formats

about.en:
Amgen Scholars Europe gives undergraduates a funded summer of hands-on research in a lab at one of five leading European institutions (ETH Zurich, Institut Pasteur, Karolinska Institutet, LMU Munich and the University of Cambridge). Scholars work on a real research project, attend seminars on science and drug discovery, and in early September everyone meets at the Amgen Scholars Europe Symposium at the University of Cambridge (travel, room and board for the symposium are covered).

about.en:
The HKU Summer Institute (HKUSI) runs short immersive programmes for students from around the world. Its new Winter Chapter takes place in Zhangjiang Science City, Shanghai's innovation hub, combining HKU-designed academic content with tech-company visits and cultural exchange.

Winter 2027 offers 'Happiness by Design: The Psychology of Wellbeing' (24–31 January, for grades 10–12 / Year 11–13) and 'Global Business Leader' (24 January – 2 February, for grades 10–12 and undergraduates in Years 1–2). Both are residential and non-credit-bearing.

en: HKU-designed programmes in Shanghai's tech hub
Psychology or business leadership tracks
Open to international secondary and early-undergraduate students

eligibility.en: Secondary students in grades 10–12 (both programmes) and undergraduates in Years 1–2 (Global Business Leader), from any country, with good English.

en: Open the HKUSI website and choose a Winter Chapter programme
Create an account in the HKUSI application system
Submit the online application and pay fees once admitted
Arrange a Chinese visa if needed

costs.en: Paid residential programme; fees listed on the HKUSI site.

about.en:
HKUSI offers a menu of summer programmes taught by HKU faculty: for secondary students (for example Technopreneurship with the HKU School of Innovation, a Chemistry Summer School, research-skills programmes) and for undergraduates/postgraduates (for example International Business in Practice with HKU Business School, Governance and Policy Leadership). Students live in HKU residences and join enrichment events across Hong Kong.

The 2027 line-up and deadlines will be published on the HKUSI site; programmes usually open for applications in winter and spring.

en: Programmes co-designed with HKU faculties
Options for secondary, undergraduate and postgraduate students
Residential experience in Hong Kong

about.en:
Penn's School of Arts & Sciences runs intensive two-week Summer Academies on the Philadelphia campus, each built around one field and taught by Penn faculty and researchers: Astronomical Techniques Research, Experimental Design, Forensic Science, Mathematics, Environmental Policy, Social Change, East Asian History, an Academic English & University Readiness Academy, and more, plus online seminars (e.g. genomics and bioinformatics, writing for researchers).

Admission is rolling until programmes are full, and only complete applications are reviewed (decisions can take up to six weeks), so applying early matters. Penn lists tuition and scholarship opportunities on its site; international students are welcome.

en: Ivy League academies taught by Penn faculty
Research-flavoured STEM tracks (astronomy, forensics, experimental design)
Rolling admission: early applicants have the most choice

eligibility.en: High-school students (grades 9–12, depending on the academy) from any country; English proficiency required (an English readiness academy is also offered).

en: Choose an academy or online seminar for summer 2027
Complete the online application (transcript, essay, recommendation as required)
Apply early: admission is rolling until full
Check scholarship opportunities and pay tuition once admitted

costs.en: Paid: tuition (and housing for residential students) per academy; see 'Tuition and Fees'. Some scholarships available.

score_reason: Strong subject academies at Penn; rolling admission; paid.
